transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Well, I guess what really made me come in is that I've started losing my place at work. I'm a receptionist, and lately, while I'm scheduling appointments or working on the lobby displays, my mind just slips off track. It's like I can't focus because I'm busy worrying about what I might have overlooked or forgotten to do. It's just getting a bit frustrating.

When your mind slips off track at work, is it because you're having worried or anxious thoughts that keep interrupting you, or does it feel more like you simply can't sustain your attention on the task itself?

It's definitely the worried thoughts interrupting me. I just find myself worrying about all kinds of ordinary things now. Work schedules, bills, travel plans, even little paperwork errors. It's like my brain gets stuck on the idea that one small mix-up could turn into a much bigger problem. So, yeah, the worry is what pulls my attention away from what I'm actually trying to do.
How long have you been experiencing this pattern of excessive worry about everyday things? Has it been going on for several months or longer?

Well, let's see... it's definitely been several months. I'd say it's been going on for about nine months now. It really started ever since this, um, overnight detention I had, and a big paperwork mix-up around it. That's when this whole pattern kind of kicked off.
When you're experiencing these worried thoughts, do you also notice physical symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, shortness of breath, or sudden intense fear that comes on quickly?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. It's not a sudden panic or anything intense like a racing heart or sweating. It's just... a constant, quiet hum of worry in the background, you know? I don't get those physical feelings you're describing.
When you're worrying about these everyday things, do you find it hard to stop worrying or control these thoughts, even when you try?

Yes, it's very hard to stop. I can tell myself, 'Sunny, it's handled,' but the thought just keeps looping. Pretty soon, I've gone from one concern to another, and I'm just checking details in my head over and over again. I just can't seem to turn it off.
Besides the difficulty concentrating at work, has this constant worry been affecting other areas of your life — like your relationships, sleep, or ability to relax and enjoy things?

Well, I'm still showing up to work and getting through the day, so I guess I'm managing. But... scheduling appointments takes me a lot longer now because I feel like I have to double-check everything I do so much. And I've even had to redo parts of the lobby displays at work because I'll just completely lose track of what I was arranging while my mind is spinning. So, it's definitely making things harder.
When you're experiencing this constant worry, do you notice any physical tension in your body — like tight muscles, headaches, or feeling fatigued or exhausted?

Yes, definitely. I mean... at the front desk, I can still smile and help people when they come in, but inside I just feel really wound tight. It's like my shoulders are constantly up around my ears, and I'm just... waiting for something to go wrong.

You mentioned the worry affects your work and concentration there. When you're at home or during your personal time, do you find yourself worrying about things in other areas of your life — like your health, finances, relationships, or other personal matters — or is the worry mostly limited to work-related things?

Well, it's definitely not just work. I find myself worrying about all kinds of ordinary things now, even when I'm at home. I'll stress over bills, or travel plans... even little paperwork errors that really shouldn't be a big deal. It just feels like if there's one small mix-up, it could turn into a much bigger problem. So, yeah, it pretty much follows me everywhere.

When you're sitting at your desk or trying to relax at home, do you find yourself feeling restless or fidgety — like you need to move around or can't stay still — or is it more just the mental tension and worry without that physical restlessness?

Um, no, not really. I don't feel like I need to get up and pace or anything. It's mostly just... like you said, the mental tension. And that tight feeling in my muscles I mentioned before. But I can sit perfectly still at my desk just fine. It's really just my brain that won't stop spinning, even when my body isn't moving.
